rules.rule: A player spawns as a single 1x1 square gem block with their nickname displayed across their main/core block.
rules.original_shows: At 00:35, the player spawns as a single 1x1 blue square gem block with their nickname ('MasterOv') displayed across it.
rules.rebuild_shows: At 00:00 of the rebuild clip, the player is already composed of multiple cyan blocks (around 4 blocks) with '+4' floating text, rather than clearly showing a 1x1 block spawn state.
rules.difference: The rebuild starts with the player already having multiple blocks attached (or instantly collecting blocks upon spawn) rather than starting and remaining briefly as a single 1x1 square gem block.
rules.fix: Ensure the player spawns as a single 1x1 square block in an area clear enough to observe the 1x1 initial state (or do not pre-attach blocks on spawn).

rules.rule: Touching small stray 1x1 blocks floating on the map attaches them to the player's block structure at the point of contact on a grid alignment.
rules.original_shows: Touching small floating 1x1 gem blocks snaps and attaches them onto the player's block structure at the grid-aligned point of contact.
rules.rebuild_shows: The player ('Tester1') moves into floating 1x1 blocks (00:00-00:02), which snap and attach onto the sides of their block structure on a grid alignment (before an AI enemy collides with the player at 00:03 and breaks them off).
rules.difference: None — the mechanic works identically; the automated test assertion only failed because an enemy collided with the player and destroyed the attached blocks before the assertion checked.
rules.fix: No game code fix needed; update the test scenario to disable or avoid enemy collisions while testing block collection.

rules.rule: When attached blocks form a complete solid square (e.g., 2x2, 3x3, 4x4, up to giant squares), they automatically merge into a single larger glossy gem block.
rules.original_shows: Blocks attach adjacent to existing blocks in a compact grid layout so they quickly form 2x2 squares and merge into larger beveled blocks.
rules.rebuild_shows: In the rebuild, some AI players have merged blocks (like Kwebbelkop and MasterOv), so merging exists, but the test player (and several AI players like Supreme) attach blocks into sprawling, branching tree-like chains instead of compact grid positions, preventing the test player from ever forming a 2x2 square during the clip (assertion failed).
rules.difference: Block attachment placement in the rebuild spreads blocks out into long branching chains rather than filling adjacent grid slots to form compact squares like in the original.
rules.fix: Fix the block attachment logic so newly collected blocks snap to the closest available grid slot to the center of mass (or compactly fill 2x2/NxN squares first) rather than branching outward into long chains.

rules.rule: Players can build complex multi-block structures with multiple merged squares of varying sizes or hollow ring shapes attached to their core block.
rules.original_shows: Players (like the large red cluster Kwebbelkop) have complex multi-block structures composed of large merged squares (e.g. 5x5, 4x4, 3x3) attached together with smaller 2x2 and 1x1 blocks around the perimeter.
rules.rebuild_shows: In the first few seconds, an orange AI player ('Kwebbelkop') is visible with a 3x3 merged square attached to smaller 1x1 blocks, and 'Jupitai' has a complex structure with a hollow ring/frame and a 2x2 block attached to 1x1s. However, the test player ('ad') stays a tiny 1x1 block and doesn't build a multi-size cluster, causing the assertion on the local player to fail.
rules.difference: The game mechanics support complex multi-block structures with varying merged square sizes as seen on the bots in the rebuild clip, but the test script didn't grow the local player into a multi-size structure to satisfy its own assertion.
rules.fix: Update the test setup for this scenario to spawn or grow the test player into a composite structure containing at least one 2x2 or 3x3 merged square alongside 1x1 blocks.

rules.rule: In the later update (Feb 2017 / mobile release), the player's core block is represented by a specific 2x2-sized Heart Block marked with a heart icon, rather than the largest merged block.
rules.original_shows: The player's core is a 2x2 block marked with a red and white heart emblem in the center, with individual 1x1 blocks attaching around it.
rules.rebuild_shows: In Heart Core mode, the player's core is a 2x2 block marked with a red and white heart emblem in the center, with 1x1 blocks attaching around it.

rules.rule: The player's block cluster moves continuously toward the mouse cursor position on PC (or virtual directional arrow on mobile).
rules.original_shows: The player's green block cluster stays centered on screen while gliding smoothly and continuously in the direction of the mouse cursor.
rules.rebuild_shows: The player's cyan block cluster stays centered on screen while gliding smoothly and continuously in the direction of the cursor (moving right, then down).
rules.difference: None regarding continuous cursor-following movement.

rules.rule: Pressing A rotates the player's block cluster counter-clockwise and pressing D rotates it clockwise.
rules.original_shows: When pressing D, the player's block cluster rotates clockwise while glowing and draining the boost meter on the bottom-left; pressing the other rotation key rotates it counter-clockwise.
rules.rebuild_shows: The player's cyan block cluster rotates clockwise (around 02s-03s) and counter-clockwise (around 03s-05s) while glowing and draining the boost meter.

rules.rule: Rotating with A or D consumes energy from the vertical green bar on the bottom-left and grants a temporary movement/rotational speed boost.
rules.original_shows: Pressing D or A rotates the block cluster, creating a glowing aura around the blocks while draining the vertical green energy bar on the bottom left. The bar regenerates when not rotating.
rules.rebuild_shows: Holding D rotates the player's blocks with a golden boost aura, draining the bottom-left energy bar (which turns yellow while draining) down to 71%, and then regenerating back to 100% green when released.
rules.difference: None significant; the core mechanic and UI feedback match.

rules.rule: In the later update (Video D), rotating/spinning causes unmerged 1x1 outer blocks to detach and fall off the player's structure.
rules.original_shows: When spinning is sustained (at ~03:23.5), unmerged 1x1 outer blocks detach and fly off tangentially.
rules.rebuild_shows: In the rebuild (00:08 - 00:12), the player spins continuously (with the yellow glow active and boost bar draining), and all outer 1x1 blocks stay firmly attached to the structure.
rules.difference: Unmerged 1x1 blocks do not detach or fly off during sustained spinning in the rebuild.
rules.fix: Ensure that when the player is spinning/rotating above the threshold (or during sustained spin), unmerged 1x1 blocks on the outer perimeter detach from the player's structure and fly off tangentially.

rules.rule: Pressing W shoots/ejects a 1x1 block from the player's structure toward the cursor, which also consumes a small amount of the green energy bar.
rules.original_shows: When pressing W (around 01:08), a 1x1 block detaches from the outer edge of the player's structure and shoots outward in the direction of the mouse cursor, coming to a stop a short distance away on the map.
rules.rebuild_shows: Around 00:04, the green energy bar drops to 99% and the player's block count decreases by 1, and a block appears briefly at the cursor/left of the player before immediately re-attaching or disappearing without visibly shooting outward and resting on the map.
rules.difference: In the rebuild, the ejected 1x1 block does not visibly travel outward from the structure toward the cursor and remain on the map as a collectible block.
rules.fix: Ensure that pressing W spawns a free 1x1 block projectile from the edge of the player's structure facing the cursor, propels it outward toward the cursor with velocity that decelerates to a stop, and prevents the player from immediately re-collecting it during the initial ejection.

rules.rule: In the initial version (Videos A, B, C, E, F, H), shooting blocks with W can break down the player's own main block into smaller blocks to regain high movement speed.
rules.original_shows: The commentator explains that having a smaller main block allows moving faster compared to a player with a huge merged block.
rules.rebuild_shows: The player collects blocks to form a 2x2 merged square (around 00:05-00:08), and then continues collecting more blocks without ever pressing W to eject or break down the merged block.
rules.difference: The test clip never exercises pressing W to eject blocks and break down the merged block.
rules.fix: Update the test script to actually press W repeatedly after forming a merged 2x2 block so the breakdown behavior can be observed.

rules.rule: Movement speed decreases as the player's main block / total mass grows larger.
rules.original_shows: A very large player (mass ~135) moving slowly across the grid, while the commentator explicitly confirms that growing bigger makes you go slower.
rules.rebuild_shows: A small player (mass 7) collecting one block (to mass 8) and then drifting around at low speed while larger AI bots move nearby.
rules.difference: The test clip in the rebuild does not grow the player significantly or compare maximum movement speeds across different sizes visually, making it impossible to verify the speed reduction from the video alone (though the programmatic assertion passed).
rules.fix: Have the test spawn or grow the player to a large mass while moving at full throttle to visually demonstrate the speed decrease.

rules.rule: The camera is top-down 2D, centered on the player's core block, and dynamically zooms out as the player's block structure grows larger.
rules.original_shows: The camera is top-down 2D, centered on the player's core block (which is rotated 45 degrees along with the world grid), and zooms out very gradually only when the player's block structure becomes huge (around 170+ blocks).
rules.rebuild_shows: In the rebuild clip, the player ('Voter1' in the center) only has a tiny structure (from 1 to 10 blocks, and then loses blocks back down to 3), yet the camera is already zoomed out way too far and continues zooming out further even as the player loses blocks or barely grows. Additionally, the world grid is axis-aligned rather than rotated 45 degrees like in the original.
rules.difference: The camera in the rebuild is much too zoomed out for a small player and appears to zoom out continuously or aggressively regardless of the actual structure radius, whereas in the original a 170-block player still fills a large portion of the screen.
rules.fix: Adjust the camera zoom formula so the base zoom is much closer for small players and only zooms out proportionally as the bounding radius of the player's attached blocks actually increases (and zooms back in if blocks are lost).

rules.rule: When two players collide, larger blocks destroy smaller blocks on contact, shattering them into collectible 1x1 blocks.
rules.original_shows: Two players (MasterOv and Ashdubhh) collide; MasterOv's large central block shatters Ashdubhh's smaller outer blocks, and eventually shatters Ashdubhh's slightly smaller core block into a burst of 1x1 red blocks.
rules.rebuild_shows: The player (VictorX) only consists of 1x1 blocks and flies around collecting gems; no collision occurs where a larger merged block shatters a smaller block on another player.
rules.difference: The test clip never demonstrates a larger block colliding with and shattering a smaller block on another player. Additionally, in the original, shattered blocks retain the color of the player they belonged to, whereas in the rebuild when bots collide off-center (e.g. MasterOv and FeralAfro around 00:04), blocks either just detach or scatter into rainbow colors.
rules.fix: Ensure the test scenario spawns two players with merged blocks of different sizes and forces them to collide so the shattering mechanic can be clearly observed. Also ensure shattered blocks burst into 1x1 collectible blocks matching the destroyed player's color.

rules.rule: In the initial version, a player dies immediately if their main (named) block is destroyed by a larger enemy block; losing outer/secondary blocks does not kill the player.
rules.original_shows: The commentator explains that if your main block dies you die, while outer blocks around you can die without killing you.
rules.rebuild_shows: At 00:04, MasterOv's large blue block collides with KingMaysam's orange blocks, shattering the orange player. However, we do not clearly see the contrast of a player losing only outer blocks and surviving vs losing the main block and dying.
rules.difference: The test clip only briefly shows one bot collision in the background and does not clearly exercise or demonstrate the distinction between losing outer blocks (surviving) and losing the main named core block (dying).
rules.fix: Create a clearer test scenario where the player (or an observed bot) first loses an outer block to a collision and survives, and then has their main named block hit by a larger block and shatters completely.

rules.rule: In the later Heart Block update (Video D), a player dies if and only if their Heart Block is destroyed.
rules.original_shows: The player has a 2x2 Heart Block at their core, which acts as their fatal life core (if damaged/destroyed, the player dies).
rules.rebuild_shows: In Heart Core mode, the player is reduced to just their 2x2 Heart Block core and survives as long as the Heart Block itself is intact.
rules.difference: None

rules.rule: White/grey square obstacle blocks are scattered throughout the arena and form a continuous perimeter wall around the map.
rules.original_shows: White/grey square obstacle blocks with rounded corners and a circular center are scattered in the arena and also form a continuous horizontal line of adjacent blocks at the map border (visible at 00:46-00:53).
rules.rebuild_shows: Scattered white/grey square obstacle blocks in the arena, with some green beveled blocks, and the test never moves near the map edge to show the perimeter wall.
rules.difference: 1) The rebuild clip never moves to the arena border to show the continuous perimeter wall of white/grey obstacle blocks. 2) The original obstacles have rounded corners and a circular inner dot, whereas the rebuild obstacles have sharp square inner shapes (and there are unexplained large green beveled blocks not in the original).
rules.fix: Ensure the perimeter wall is constructed out of the white/grey obstacle blocks (and update the test to move near the border so it is visible). Style the obstacle blocks with rounded outer corners and a circular inner recess to match the original.

rules.rule: If a player's outer/secondary block touches a white obstacle block, that block explodes/shatters into small 1x1 blocks; if the player's main/core block touches a white obstacle block in the early version, the player dies or their main block shatters.
rules.original_shows: In the original clip, when an outer block of the player's structure touches a white obstacle block (around 01:43), that outer block detaches/shatters off the player while the white obstacle block remains intact and stationary on the map. Furthermore, loose 1x1 collectible blocks floating around the map can pass through/sit inside the white obstacle without anything happening.
rules.rebuild_shows: In the rebuild, neither the player's main core block nor any of the player's attached secondary blocks ever touch a white obstacle block during the clip. Also, at 00:05, a white obstacle block disappears when loose 1x1 blocks touch it.
rules.difference: 1) The test did not actually drive the player into a white obstacle block to demonstrate shattering of player blocks. 2) White obstacle blocks in the rebuild are destroyed/disappear when loose 1x1 blocks touch them, whereas in the original white obstacles are permanent/indestructible obstacles that only shatter attached player blocks on contact.
rules.fix: Ensure white obstacle blocks are not destroyed by loose 1x1 blocks or player collisions, and update the test scenario so the player's attached outer blocks (and core block) actually collide with a white obstacle block to verify they shatter into 1x1 blocks.

rules.rule: If a white obstacle block is hit enough times, it is destroyed and disappears from the map.
rules.original_shows: In the original clip, when a player's blocks collide with the white obstacle blocks (squares with inner squares), both the player's block and the white obstacle block are destroyed and disappear from the map (e.g., at 06:06 and 06:10).
rules.rebuild_shows: In the rebuild clip, the player ('Tester') and AI bots move around the map, occasionally passing near white obstacle blocks, and at 00:05 an orange AI bot hits a white obstacle block and loses a piece, while the white obstacle block gets a crack/damage indicator on it, but no white obstacle block is hit enough times to be completely destroyed and disappear.
rules.difference: The test clip never actually hits a white obstacle block enough times to destroy it, so we only see the damaged/cracked state at 00:05 and never see one disappear. Additionally, in the original, a single collision with a player block destroys the white obstacle block immediately, whereas in the rebuild it takes multiple hits (showing a crack first).
rules.fix: Ensure white obstacle blocks are destroyed on collision (or update the test to hit the obstacle enough times to verify it disappears, and check if obstacles should have 1 HP like in the original clip).

rules.rule: In the later update (Video D), large neutral colored gem blocks ('food blocks') spawn around the map; players with sufficiently large blocks can ram them to shatter them into a cluster of collectible 1x1 blocks.
rules.original_shows: In the original (Clip 1), the player's ship has large merged blocks (3x3 and 2x2). When it rams into a large pink gem block ('food block'), the gem block shatters into a large cluster of 1x1 collectible pink/white blocks that scatter across the area and are then sucked in and collected by the player.
rules.rebuild_shows: In the rebuild (Clip 2), there is a large green gem block and a large pink gem block on the map. However: 1) None of the ships in the clip have merged 2x2+ blocks (merge mechanics are either disabled or missing in this mode, as players just have sprawling chains of 1x1 blocks around their core). 2) At 00:05-00:08, the orange player ('PoxiePro') collides with the large green gem block using 1x1 blocks, and nothing happens (or the test never actually tests ramming it with a 2x2+ block to shatter it). Furthermore, the background in Video D is dark grid, whereas the rebuild shows the light grid.
rules.difference: The rebuild clip never demonstrates a large neutral gem block being shattered into a cluster of 1x1 gems by a 2x2+ block (in fact, players in the rebuild clip don't even have 2x2+ merged blocks). Also, when the orange player's 1x1 blocks hit the green gem block, they just pass through/overlap with it rather than bouncing off or shattering it.
rules.fix: Ensure block merging (2x2, 3x3, etc.) is active in this game mode, ensure solid collision with giant gem blocks for small blocks, and ensure that ramming a giant gem block with a 2x2+ block shatters it into a scattered burst of 1x1 collectible food blocks (and make sure the test scenario actually triggers this shatter in the recording).

rules.rule: Each 1x1 block attached to the player's structure equals 1 point of score, which is tracked in real time on the leaderboard.
rules.original_shows: As the player (MasterOv) collects individual 1x1 blocks, their score on the top-right leaderboard (bottom entry, #18/#16/#14/#13) increases by 1 per block in real time (from 1 to 2, 3, 4, 6, 7).
rules.rebuild_shows: As the player (Tester1) collects individual 1x1 blocks, their score on the top-right leaderboard (#11 Tester1) increases by 1 per block in real time (from 4 to 7, 8, 9), matching the exact count of attached 1x1 cells.

rules.rule: In the later update (Video D), large players experience slow score decay (losing approximately 1 block per second) to prevent passive camping.
rules.original_shows: A very large player (score around 1500) experiencing score decay, ticking down by 1 block per second.
rules.rebuild_shows: A small player (score 7 to 13) collecting blocks; no large players (near 1500+ score) are present or shown experiencing score decay.
rules.difference: The test did not set up or show a large player to demonstrate the score decay mechanic.
rules.fix: Update the test scenario to spawn or grow a player to a large size (e.g. >1000 score) so that the score decay and block shedding can be observed.

rules.rule: The HUD displays a 4-quadrant minimap in the top-left showing player dots, a vertical green energy/power bar (0 to 100) in the bottom-left, and a Top 10 leaderboard plus the player's current rank and score in the top-right.
rules.original_shows: Top-left minimap with 4 quadrants and player dots, bottom-left vertical green energy bar with number on top, top-right leaderboard showing top 10 plus player's own rank below.
rules.rebuild_shows: Top-left 4-quadrant minimap with player dots, bottom-left vertical green energy bar with 100% label, top-right neon leaderboard showing top 10 and player's own rank/score below.
rules.difference: None significant; all three HUD components match layout and function.

rules.rule: Players can select free cosmetic skins (solid colors or YouTuber/creator logos such as Kwebbelkop, MasterOv, Jelly, Slogoman, AzzyLand, FaZe Mojo) from the Skin menu, which apply to every merged square block in their structure.
rules.original_shows: Clicking SKIN opens a full-screen white/grey diamond-patterned background screen with floating left and right blue arrow buttons on either side of the central block preview, and a cyan SAVE button below it. Cycling through shows solid colors and custom creator/YouTuber avatar icons.
rules.rebuild_shows: Clicking SKIN opens an overlay box with a solid white border around the block preview, a text label ('Cyan Crystal') underneath the block, and boxed arrow buttons.
rules.difference: The skin selection screen layout in the rebuild uses a white card container and displays a skin name text label, whereas the original displays the block preview, arrows, and SAVE button directly on the patterned background without a card container or text label. Also, the test clip only showed cycling once to 'Cyan Crystal' and didn't show the creator/YouTuber logo skins in the selector (though bots in-game have names like Kwebbelkop/MasterOv with solid color blocks rather than logo skins).
rules.fix: Remove the white card container and text label from the skin selector UI so the preview block, left/right arrows, and SAVE button sit directly over the patterned background, and ensure creator logo image skins are present and applied to blocks.

rules.rule: The settings menu allows players to toggle a Dark Background theme and select a server region (Europe Frankfurt/London, N. America East/Central/West/South, Asia Tokyo/Singapore).
rules.original_shows: Clicking the green gear button next to the SKIN and PLAY GAME buttons opens a settings panel below with a 'Dark Background' checkbox and a server region dropdown (showing Europe Frankfurt, N. America East/West/Central/South, Europe London, Asia Tokyo/Singapore).
rules.rebuild_shows: Clicking the green gear button opens a settings panel below the main buttons with a 'Dark Background' checkbox and a server region dropdown, and toggling Dark Background changes the arena grid from light to dark charcoal.

rules.rule: The game supports cross-platform multiplayer between web browsers (PC) and mobile devices (iOS/Android), as well as Party codes (Create/Join) and Free For All / Teams modes.
rules.original_shows: The original main menu shows a 'Play with your friends in the same map!' box in the top right with CREATE and JOIN buttons.
rules.rebuild_shows: Two live player clients (Tester1 and Tester2) are connected in the same multiplayer arena interacting with each other, and at 00:08 of clip 1 the main menu shows the top-right box with CREATE and JOIN buttons and a generated party room code ('Room: PARTY-5NCU (Copied!)').
rules.difference: None

rules.rule: In the later update (Video D), popping/collecting sound effects play when picking up small blocks or shattering large blocks.
rules.original_shows: In the original clip, the commentator mentions and demonstrates sound effects added in the update while collecting blocks.
rules.rebuild_shows: The rebuild plays synthesized popping and chime sound effects via WebAudio when collecting small 1x1 blocks and merging squares, as verified by the passing assertion and visual feedback.
rules.difference: None
